scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic vault transition credits an internal user ledger without the matching issued-unit update, so the formal conservation equation becomes false at the committed post-state.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A local test chain with synthetic accounts, bounded test tokens, a shadow ledger, and read-only state snapshots evaluates only the conservation predicate and creates no real-value effect.
scenarios.positive_control: The same bounded deposit transition with both ledger and issued-unit updates applied preserves the explicit conservation equation at the identical commit observation point.
scenarios.negative_control: A transaction that fails its deposit precondition reverts before state commitment and therefore leaves the pre-state conservation predicate unchanged.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if validation would transact with real funds, touch public protocol state, manipulate a live oracle/market/governance path, or leave the owned local test chain.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After atomically binding ledger and issued-unit updates, replay from the same local snapshot preserves conservation and all intended synthetic deposit controls still succeed.
scenarios.protocol_deployment_state_generation: Record protocol identity, local chain reset, deployment/configuration generation, contract revision, pre-state snapshot, transaction generation, and post-state generation.
scenarios.invariant_domain_observation_point: Bind the invariant identity to the complete synthetic vault accounting domain, define the conservation equation and tolerance, and evaluate it only after the transaction commit point.
scenarios.entrypoint_actor_transition_trace: Record the synthetic depositor, role state, deposit entrypoint, preconditions, ordered ledger/supply writes, first omitted matching update, commit, and post-state receipt.
scenarios.asset_accounting_conservation_state: Track bounded test-token balance, internal user ledger, issued units, reserve/backing, fee/rounding domain, and the exact before/after conservation equation.
scenarios.external_dependency_assumption_state: Use a fixed-behavior fake test token with deterministic transfer semantics and record that no callback, oracle, upgrade, or external market behavior participates.
scenarios.reachability_violation_witness: From a deterministic local snapshot, replay the exact bounded deposit sequence and capture the first committed state where the explicit conservation predicate becomes false.
scenarios.downstream_protocol_consumer_identity: Identify the shadow accounting consumer that reads the committed ledger and issued-unit state and emits a read-only invariant receipt for the same transaction generation.
scenarios.effective_invariant_break_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to one synthetic local accounting state in which ledger and issued-unit totals violate the stated conservation predicate.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a local read-only receipt containing pre/post totals, invariant equation, first invalid state delta, and no transferable real asset or production effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate chain reset, deployment, actor, transaction, contract revision, state snapshots, invariant identity, accounting domain, violation witness, and receipt deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold deployment, actor, test-token behavior, amount, and observation point constant while changing only the omitted issued-unit update versus the correct atomic update.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject fee/dust/rounding omissions, reverted transactions, transient pre-commit state, fake-token contract drift, wrong deployment revision, or receipt from another chain reset.
scenarios.evidence_level: SCI4 because a reversible synthetic accounting state at the commit point is causally bound to the exact ledger/supply transition that falsifies conservation.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: SCI4 maximum until complete external-assumption provenance, alternative elimination, deterministic remediation replay, and regression evidence satisfy the SCI5 contract.

scenarios.hypothesis: A toy claim system reuses claimed-state identity across epoch generations so one synthetic claim identifier can be accepted again when the invariant requires uniqueness across the bound domain.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled local test chain and read-only claim ledger use fake identifiers and inert claim markers only; no token transfer, external payout, or real account receives value.
scenarios.positive_control: A current epoch-scoped claim key that includes the required uniqueness generation rejects the second synthetic claim while allowing a distinct valid claim.
scenarios.negative_control: An intentionally reusable claim class documented as per-epoch remains valid across epochs, proving the harness distinguishes global uniqueness from permitted epoch reuse.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if validation would transact with real funds, touch public protocol state, manipulate a live oracle/market/governance path, or leave the owned local test chain.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After binding claim identity to the required uniqueness domain/generation, replay rejects the duplicate synthetic claim while documented distinct or per-epoch claims remain valid.
scenarios.protocol_deployment_state_generation: Record protocol/deployment revision, local chain reset, epoch generation, claim-ledger generation, synthetic actor, transaction generations, and before/after state snapshots.
scenarios.invariant_domain_observation_point: Define the one-time/uniqueness invariant, whether its scope is global or epoch-bound, the claim-key fields, and evaluate it at successful claim commit.
scenarios.entrypoint_actor_transition_trace: Capture claimant identity, claim entrypoint, current epoch, lookup key generation, claimed-state check, state write, commit, and first transition permitting the duplicate.
scenarios.asset_accounting_conservation_state: Use an inert claim marker rather than an asset payout and record that no balance, debt, reserve, share, or external accounting effect is required for the uniqueness witness.
scenarios.external_dependency_assumption_state: Keep external dependencies absent or fixed and record that no callback, oracle, token hook, upgrade transition, or asynchronous bridge state explains duplicate acceptance.
scenarios.reachability_violation_witness: Replay two bounded local claim transactions from the same deterministic fixture and capture the second committed acceptance that falsifies the explicit uniqueness predicate.
scenarios.downstream_protocol_consumer_identity: Identify the local claim-state consumer that accepts the second claim and emits a read-only receipt naming claim identity, epoch generation, and prior claimed state.
scenarios.effective_invariant_break_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to duplicate acceptance of one inert synthetic claim marker under the wrong uniqueness/epoch generation binding.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a deterministic local receipt showing first and second claim commits, claim-key generations, uniqueness predicate, and no real payout or asset transfer.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Bind chain reset, deployment, epoch, claimant, claim identifier, two transaction generations, claimed-state versions, invariant result, consumer, and receipt.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold claimant, claim identifier, entrypoint, deployment, and transaction ordering constant while changing only stale/reused versus correctly epoch/domain-bound claim identity.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject documented per-epoch reuse, failed first claim, reverted second transaction, changed claim domain, another deployment/epoch, or receipt miscorrelation.
scenarios.evidence_level: SCI3 because a bounded local transaction sequence reaches a committed state where the explicit synthetic claim-uniqueness predicate is false without real-value consequence.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: SCI3 maximum until a bounded reversible protocol-state effect plus full generation provenance and remediation replay justify SCI4 or SCI5.

scenarios.hypothesis: A toy protocol advances from a collection phase to a settled phase before a documented pending-accounting predicate is satisfied, creating an illegal committed state transition.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A local test-chain phase machine with synthetic queue entries and a shadow settlement counter exposes only read-only phase/accounting receipts and no real assets or external contracts.
scenarios.positive_control: The same phase transition after all synthetic pending entries are settled advances normally and the legal-state-transition invariant remains true at commit.
scenarios.negative_control: While pending entries remain, an explicit guard blocks phase advancement and preserves the collection phase without mutating the settlement state.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if validation would transact with real funds, touch public protocol state, manipulate a live oracle/market/governance path, or leave the owned local test chain.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After requiring the settlement predicate at the transition boundary, the invalid advance is rejected while the fully settled positive control still reaches the next phase.
scenarios.protocol_deployment_state_generation: Record local deployment/configuration, phase generation, queue generation, settlement-state generation, actor, transition transaction, and pre/post snapshots.
scenarios.invariant_domain_observation_point: Define the legal phase-transition invariant and required pending-accounting predicate, including the terminal observation point after phase-state commit.
scenarios.entrypoint_actor_transition_trace: Capture the synthetic actor, finalize/advance entrypoint, pending-state precondition, ordered accounting and phase writes, skipped check, commit, and illegal post-phase.
scenarios.asset_accounting_conservation_state: Track bounded synthetic queue totals, settled/pending counters, any shadow ledger amounts, and prove the witness is phase/accounting consistency rather than asset movement.
scenarios.external_dependency_assumption_state: Use no external dependency or a fixed fake dependency and record that callbacks, oracles, tokens, upgrade state, and timing services cannot explain the phase violation.
scenarios.reachability_violation_witness: From a deterministic snapshot with one pending synthetic entry, invoke the bounded advance operation and capture the committed settled phase while the required predicate remains false.
scenarios.downstream_protocol_consumer_identity: Identify the local phase-state consumer that observes the committed phase and pending counter together and emits the invariant violation receipt.
scenarios.effective_invariant_break_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to one reversible local illegal phase transition with an outstanding synthetic accounting obligation.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a local state/receipt pair showing phase generation, pending count, first invalid transition, and no production, financial, or governance consequence.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate deployment, phase/queue generations, actor, transaction, pending predicate, ordered state writes, post-state, consumer, and receipt deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold deployment, actor, queue contents, and target phase constant while changing only whether required settlement state is completed before the phase transition.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject intentionally optional settlement, permitted transient phase semantics, reverted transition, stale snapshot, asynchronous completion contract, or another phase generation.
scenarios.evidence_level: SCI4 because a reversible local phase marker is committed while its required accounting predicate is false and the exact skipped transition is causally identified.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: SCI4 maximum until complete alternative elimination, dependency provenance, remediation replay, and regression evidence satisfy the SCI5 requirements.

scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic solvency predicate counts reserves and settled debt but omits a bounded pending liability generation, allowing a committed state to appear solvent under a partial accounting domain.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled local test chain and shadow solvency model use synthetic reserve/debt/liability numbers and read-only predicates only, with no real token market or transferable asset.
scenarios.positive_control: The complete solvency predicate including pending liabilities correctly rejects or marks the same synthetic state insolvent according to the documented bound.
scenarios.negative_control: A state with the same reserves and no pending liability passes both partial and complete predicates, proving the harness is not forcing a failure.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if validation would transact with real funds, touch public protocol state, manipulate a live oracle/market/governance path, or leave the owned local test chain.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After binding pending liabilities into the accounting domain, the solvency check matches the shadow model while genuinely solvent synthetic states still pass.
scenarios.protocol_deployment_state_generation: Record protocol/deployment revision, local chain reset, accounting epoch, reserve/debt/pending-liability generations, check transaction, and state snapshots.
scenarios.invariant_domain_observation_point: Define the solvency invariant as a complete reserve-versus-liability equation, state its units/tolerance, and evaluate at the documented post-accounting observation point.
scenarios.entrypoint_actor_transition_trace: Capture the synthetic accounting/check entrypoint, actor, pre-state, liability creation, solvency evaluation, commit/decision point, and first state/decision using the incomplete predicate.
scenarios.asset_accounting_conservation_state: Bind synthetic reserves, settled debt, pending liabilities, fee/rounding domains, and the full shadow solvency equation to the same accounting epoch.
scenarios.external_dependency_assumption_state: Use fixed local values with no price oracle or external token dependency so the case isolates accounting-domain completeness rather than external-data trust.
scenarios.reachability_violation_witness: Replay the bounded liability-creation and solvency-check sequence and capture the deterministic state where the partial predicate passes while the complete invariant is false.
scenarios.downstream_protocol_consumer_identity: Identify the local solvency decision consumer that trusts the partial predicate and emits a read-only receipt with reserve, debt, pending liability, and decision.
scenarios.effective_invariant_break_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to one synthetic local solvency decision computed from an incomplete accounting domain, without real lending or asset release.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a read-only local solvency receipt containing complete/partial equations, accounting generations, observed decision, and no external financial effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Bind chain/deployment, accounting epoch, reserve/debt/liability generations, actor, transaction, predicate versions, consumer decision, and receipt deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold reserves, settled debt, pending liability amount, deployment, and consumer constant while changing only omission versus inclusion of the pending-liability domain.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject fee/rounding tolerance, pending liability not yet contractually effective, oracle/value conversion differences, reverted state, or receipt from another accounting epoch.
scenarios.evidence_level: SCI3 because a reachable local decision uses a partial accounting predicate while the explicit complete solvency invariant is deterministically false.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: SCI3 maximum until a bounded reversible protocol-state effect plus complete accounting provenance and remediation regression justify SCI4 or SCI5.
